chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from Aban, from Sulayman ibn 'Abdillah al-Hashimi, from his father, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed to a man [executor], so he gave him one thousand dirhams as the charity of his wealth, and it was lost from the executor. He said: 'He [the executor] is liable [for it], and he does not return [claim it back] from the heirs.'
ai.seo_question: Is the executor personally liable if he loses the deceased's charity funds?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that the executor acts as a guarantor (damin) for the specific charity funds entrusted to him, bearing the risk of loss personally rather than passing it to the heirs. This ruling underscores the fiduciary responsibility of the *wasi* in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring that charitable bequests are fulfilled from the executor's own pocket if the assets are lost during his custody.
